title: Lumbopelvic ratio L/P during straight-leg lifting (trunk extension from 90 deg), by trunk-angle range, load and velocity
condition: healthy, standing, straight-leg lift from 90 deg trunk flexion to upright, 0.1 or 10 kg in front of the body, 15/30/60 deg/s

quantity.name: lumbopelvic ratio L/P
quantity.definition: Pelvis P = S1 skin sensor sagittal angle; total trunk T = T10 skin sensor angle, both from relaxed upright (zero); lumbar L = T - P (T10-S1). L/P = mean ratio of lumbar to pelvic angle within each trunk-angle range (mean of ratios over subjects/trials; large SD because P is small near upright).

source.sample: 18 healthy adults (13M, 5F), no history of LBP, trunk flexion > 90 deg
source.citation_note: DOI not printed in the PDF; not filled

protocol.summary: Isokinetic trunk extension (straight legs) from a static 90 deg flexed posture to upright with the load at waist level, tracking a moving target at 15, 30 or 60 deg/s, lifting 0.1 or 10 kg in front of the body; electromagnetic sensors (Ascension) over S1 and T10 at 44 Hz.
how_to_use: Pick the trunk-angle range (T10 inclination from upright) of the posture to model.
Split trunk flexion as pelvis = T/(1+L/P), lumbar (T10-S1) = T - pelvis.
These are lifting (extension) ratios; for unloaded forward flexion use the flexion-phase tests (Tafazzol 2014, Ghasemi 2021).
Load raised L/P (2.13 -> 2.45, P<0.05); the range values pool both loads and all velocities.
SDs are very large (mean of ratios); use for robustness runs, not as a tight target.

measurement.device: Ascension Technology sensors taped over S1 and T10 spinous processes, 44 Hz
measurement.task: trunk extension from 90 deg to upright at 15/30/60 deg/s with 0.1 or 10 kg in front

protocol.notes: Lumbar angle spans T10-S1 (includes T10-T12). Fig 2 (L/P by weight x velocity) and Figs 3-4 (eigenvector-model L vs P curves, model fits) not extracted. Table 1 range labels are 5-30/30-60/60-90 deg (text says 0-30).

data.basis: mean L/P within trunk-angle range, pooled over weight and velocity
